title: Metals and non-metals: properties compared
examples: What are the properties of metals?
How are metals different from non-metals?

explain.say: Think of a steel spoon and a lump of charcoal. One shines and bends; the other is dull and crumbles. Look at the board. You can see the two big teams chemists split the elements into: metals and non-metals.

See the metals side? Metals are shiny, and they let heat and electricity flow through them easily. That is called conducting. That is why your pan heats up fast and wires are copper. Can you name a metal in your kitchen?

Now look at the non-metals side. Most are dull and do not conduct well, so we call them insulators, which means they block heat or electricity. Many are gases, like oxygen and nitrogen. Can you think of a non-metal you breathe?

Oxygen! Now look at the sorting on the board. Iron, copper, gold and aluminium are metals. Oxygen, carbon, sulfur and chlorine are non-metals. One tricky one: mercury is a metal, yet it is a liquid! Did you know that?

Great sorting! There is an odd one on this side too: graphite, a kind of carbon, is a non-metal that conducts, so your pencil line can carry a tiny current. Wow: more than three quarters of all the elements are metals.

faq.a: Metals have electrons that are free to move through the whole metal. When you connect a battery, these electrons flow, carrying the current.
asks: Why are wires made of metal?

faq.a: An insulator is a material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily. Most non-metals, like sulfur, and plastics are insulators.
Yes. Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature. It is shiny and conducts electricity, like other metals.
Yes. Graphite is a form of carbon, a non-metal, but it has electrons free to move along its layers, so it conducts.

faq.q: What do metal oxides and non-metal oxides do in water?
faq.a: Metal oxides that dissolve make alkaline solutions. Non-metal oxides, like carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide, make acidic solutions.
asks: Are metal oxides acidic or basic?

facts: More than three quarters of the known elements are metals.
Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

quiz.show: A shiny solid conducts electricity and bends without breaking. What is it most likely to be?
quiz.why: Shiny, conducting and bendable are typical metal properties.
